title: Subsequence Sum After Capping Elements
summary: Given an integer array nums of size n and a positive integer k, for each integer x from 1 to n, determine if it is possible to select a subsequence from the array where each element is capped by x (i.e., each element is replaced by the minimum of the element and x) such that the sum of the elements in the subsequence equals k.
statement: Given an integer array nums of size n and a positive integer k, for each integer x from 1 to n, determine if it is possible to select a subsequence from the array where each element is capped by x (i.e., each element is replaced by the minimum of the element and x) such that the sum of the elements in the subsequence equals k. Return a boolean array of size n, where the i-th element is true if such a subsequence exists when x = i + 1, and false otherwise.
constraints: One to 4,000 values, each between one and n; k is at most 4,000.
For every cap x from one through n, replace each value by min(value,x).
Return whether a nonempty subsequence can sum exactly to k.
reference_solution:
def capped_subsequence_sum_possible(nums,k):
    n=len(nums);counts=[0]*(n+1)
    for value in nums:counts[value]+=1
    reachable=1;remaining=n;answer=[];mask=(1<<(k+1))-1
    for cap in range(1,n+1):
        possible=False
        for capped_count in range(min(remaining,k//cap)+1):
            target=k-capped_count*cap
            if reachable>>target&1:possible=True;break
        answer.append(possible)
        for _ in range(counts[cap]):reachable=(reachable|(reachable<<cap))&mask
        remaining-=counts[cap]
    return answer

hints: At cap x, values below x keep their value and every remaining value contributes exactly x.
Maintain subset sums of values already below the cap and try t capped elements for k-t*x.
Use a bitset for processed values; answer the cap, then insert values equal to x and reduce the remaining count.
Every capped subsequence uniquely splits into processed original values and t still-capped values, so the test is exact.
